name: inject_v1
_comment: Supervised training on MANUFACTURED pairs. A group's deepest stack is the target; the input is that target plus a scaled field of the camera's own noise, built by cancelling the sky between two disjoint half-stacks. This is no longer Noise2Noise -- see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-noise-injection-training-design.md. It exists because at 250-450 frames there was nothing in the archive cleaner than Andreas' own stacks, so the lesson was empty and n2n_v2 learned to do nothing (55% of the noise removed on M45 where GraXpert removes 85%).
_comment_dataset: Selects data.InjectionDataset for TRAINING only. The do-no-harm gate keeps judging on the REAL held-out pairs the ladder below builds: manufactured data judging a model trained on manufactured data is a closed loop that cannot detect its own premise being wrong.
_comment_held_out: NEVER training material: M8 and M45 are Andreas' own masters and the only honest tests this project has; NGC6888 and NGC281 are the gate's held-out pairs. build_injection.plan_groups refuses to build them and data.split_injection_tiles refuses to load them. NGC7023 moves from validation into TRAINING here -- its 821 frames make it one of only three groups able to supply a genuinely clean target -- and M27 validates alone.
_comment_sensor: TWO DIFFERENT THINGS. `sensor` is the model's identity: stage() writes denoise_{sensor}_v1.onnx and the S30 Pro is the camera Nocturne targets. `sensors` is the training MATERIAL, and the S50 groups are the deep ones (M42 2361 frames, SH2-142 1357, NGC7023 821) -- which is exactly where a clean target has to come from.
_comment_ladder: Everything below drives the LADDER build, which this run needs only for the gate's real held-out pairs. The values are n2n_v2's unchanged, so those pairs -- and therefore every per-target gate metric -- stay comparable run to run.
